primary_prs.title: Exhibit a nonsymmetric width-eight BIT projector link (no κ)
primary_prs.head: f967555200c111925d48a46b65b124432a762b65
primary_prs.body:
## Summary

A nonsymmetric rank-one idempotent joins two fixed normal-form triples over F2 at width eight. The complete pool contains seven projectors, its off-diagonal pattern space has dimension five and contains no matrix unit, and its seven-dimensional joint image is irreducible. This is a scoped construction with a written proof and exact finite corroboration.

The new link has image `x = e2 + e5 + e6` and covector `y = e2 + e5 + e6 + e7`. The off-diagonal row and column at coordinate 6 force this link throughout its pattern coset. Coordinate 7 enters only on the covector side, so the incidence on the joint image agrees with the square-link construction of #7281.

This answers Open next question 3 of #7281 at `0cd5324c41490b856d0e94daa8b011683fc153f6`. The proof cites its complete-pool calculation for the two blocks. The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit unpaidmoon for #7281, #7237 and the normal-form triple in #6921, and Nick Petalas for the #5921 fiber lemma used in #7281. The package records the proof hash and exact source links.

Canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. Card `bit-new-register-model` changes scope to the fixed-block BIT geometry question. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693301).

## Evidence

- #7281's width-eight census treated symmetric links. The new verifier tests membership in this particular pattern space against all 32,640 width-eight rank-one idempotents.
- Both verifier modes return `PASS_NO_EDGE_ASYMMETRIC_BLOCK_LINK` with 31 nonzero patterns, 7 projectors, 127 spanning orbits and 2 controls. Each registered command took 0.03 seconds on local CPython 3.12.15. Metadata and pins, registered replay, committed bytes and source history, and export integrity and input coverage all passed.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -B -W error -X dev research/no-edge-asymmetric-block-link/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -B -W error -X dev research/no-edge-asymmetric-block-link/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/no-edge-asymmetric-block-link
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/no-edge-asymmetric-block-link --check-source-history
```

Substitute any CPython 3.12 installation for that path. The verifier uses only the standard library.

The proof treats one pattern space at width eight with the two fixed blocks. Classification of extensions, realization by a paid BIT word, and native and supplier obligations remain open. No new κ is claimed. Predecessor verifiers, the selected scientific replay, Lean and Docker were unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

primary_prs.title: Prove a forward slack floor for exact-sum Gaussian rounding (no κ)
primary_prs.head: 317fecee459888f4e4fecd8ca62adeb7583f696d
primary_prs.body:
## Summary

**Scoped proof with an exact finite witness.** An injective Gaussian-pair rounder that preserves the exact sum and has Euclidean error at most one needs forward outward norm slack at least `sqrt(5)-sqrt(3)`. In the sum-one fiber, eight inputs of squared norm at most five have only six distinct legal outputs under a strictly smaller bound. An explicit matching attains equality on those eight inputs.

The lower bound uses no square identity, phase covariance, periodicity or surjectivity. Global attainment, physical implementation and an actual caller binding remain open. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. aliromman's #6509 supplies the ideal pair and exact-sum contract. CubeJerry's #7570 supplies the fixed-sum context and leaves this forward lower bound open. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693314)

## Evidence and reproduction

Normal and optimized CPython 3.12.15 checks enumerate 32 error-one edges, 16 strict edges to six outputs, four threshold edges and the eight-edge matching. Both direct modes and the registered package replay pass locally. The committed-byte and source-history preflight passes. The two registered commands took 0.01 and 0.02 seconds when timed directly on macOS arm64.

From the repository root, with CPython 3.12 and its standard library. The first line records the exact local interpreter path. At another checkout, use the local CPython 3.12 path.

```sh
py=/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
pkg=research/gaussian-exact-sum-forward-slack
"$py" -B scripts/research_package.py --package "$pkg"
"$py" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package "$pkg" --check-source-history
"$py" -W error -B "$pkg/verify.py"
"$py" -W error -O -B "$pkg/verify.py"
```

Expected statuses are `PASS_GAUSSIAN_EXACT_SUM_FORWARD_SLACK`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Open next questions

Can a global exact-sum map attain `sqrt(5)-sqrt(3)`? A first step is to check complete neighborhoods beyond squared norm five at this exact threshold. The square-to-swap construction gives a global upper bound of `sqrt(19)-sqrt(13)`. [#7570 proof](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/blob/053c42c68165cf24fd4e8bc33c2b20d6ac3d399b/research/sharp-order-four-gaussian-rounding/proof/PROOF.md)

## Related open work

- The unrestricted bilateral optimum is 1/2. Its construction leaves the exact-sum contract open. [#7569](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7569)
- The sharp square-to-swap result imposes an additional algebraic identity and supplies a global upper bound for the exact-sum class. [#7570](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7570)
- The finite Hall thresholds concern the unrestricted rounding graph. Here all edges stay in the sum-one fiber. [#7571](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/75

primary_prs.title: Prove the exact correction rank for paired support maps (no κ)
primary_prs.head: 0438595fadc4902fa20cb88aecc305b526193a99
primary_prs.body:
## Summary

This scoped algebraic proof gives the exact minimum of rank(P − I) for invertible P with prescribed primal restriction f:S→V and prescribed inverse-transpose action on dual support. Write the dual constraint as πP = g, with g and π surjective and πf = g|S. With d(s) = f(s) − s, the minimum is

~~~text
rank(g − π) + rank(d) − min(rank(πd), rank(gd)).
~~~

The proof constructs an attaining fixed subspace, then completes bases of the two quotient maps. A two-dimensional contract needs rank two for invertibility and rank one if singular completions are allowed. The theorem and example hold over every field. [Written proof](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/61ce91fbf49b60a912b3728cbab47561615768c8/research/primal-dual-completion-rank/PROOF.md).

This settles the algebraic optimization in GQ08 of Dugongue's atlas. G16 and G17 supply the support extension and low-rank inverse setting. aliromman's dyadic helper-basis completion is a related implementation for one normalized primal and dual pair. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. [Atlas #5803](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5803), [dyadic precedent #5611](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5611), [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693317).

## Evidence

- GQ08 leaves the completion parameters free. The proof gives an exact lower bound and a construction attaining it for any compatible paired support contract.
- The verifier enumerated every binary matrix through dimension three. All 21,354 normalized contracts agreed with both formulas, including 2,022 with a strict increase. The explicit rank-one versus rank-two fixture passed, and the check rejected a missing invertibility charge.
- Both registered commands passed with CPython 3.12.15 and printed `PASS_PRIMAL_DUAL_COMPLETION_RANK`. Their direct runs took 0.19 seconds each. The package runner printed `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The six-file committed-byte, mode and source-history check printed `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.
- The committed export and declared-input checks passed. Both direct modes ran from the read-only Git-free copy, with the same output as the checkout and with all exported hashes preserved.

From the repository root, with CPython 3.12:

~~~sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/primal-dual-completion-rank/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/primal-dual-completion-rank/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/primal-dual-completion-rank

~~~

primary_prs.title: Classify rectangular Gaussian monomial symmetries (no κ)
primary_prs.head: 82f6d6ac7cb248a4996452ca23cc0695ae5682e2
primary_prs.body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with finite exact corroboration. For an exact Gaussian matrix $G$ between two Cartesian grids, every monomial pair satisfying $UG=GV$ uses the same signed coordinate permutation on both grids. Two axes can exchange exactly when their row lengths, column lengths and effective weights $\gamma_i s_i t_i$ agree. The monomial weights are then determined up to a common nonzero scalar.

CubeJerry's [#7597](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7597) treats the matching square centralizer and leaves rectangular or independently indexed blocks open. The mixed four-entry ratio gives the two affine maps without identifying the row and column index sets. The resulting classification covers different grid sizes, origins and spacings, with arbitrary invertible complex diagonal gauges.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. The package credits CubeJerry's square invariant and orbit work, and the established paired monomial symmetry framework. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693332).

## Evidence

- The verifier tries all **18,444** row/column permutation pairs in four small fixtures and separately verifies **34** explicit monomial lifts across five fixtures. The $8\times12$ example allows an axis exchange even though the two Gaussian weights and their corresponding row spacings differ.
- It checks **1,836** lifted endpoint entries and four controls for independent reflections, omitted gauges, a changed monomial weight and the zero-weight boundary.
- Standard-library CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64. Direct normal and optimized replay produced identical output in 0.37 s and 0.35 s. Both registered commands and the committed-byte/source-history check passed locally.

From the repository root:

~~~sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/rectangular-gaussian-monomial/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/rectangular-gaussian-monomial/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/rectangular-gaussian-monomial
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/rectangular-gaussian-monomial --check-source-history
~~~

Any CPython 3.12 executable can replace the absolute path. Expected markers are PASS_RECTANGULAR_GAUSSIAN_MONOMIAL, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES.

## Limitations

The theorem fixes full Cartesian grids, positive diagonal Gaussian weights and unrounded entries. Matching a physical source block, including periodic aliases or nonseparable phases, remains open. No physical gauge, layout, precision, tape or recovery cost is established. The five selected framework assumptions remain. No new κ or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. primary_prs.head: d9db97d5075fa6dd28002f54fd139f94f98935e8
primary_prs.body:
Lean-only package, part 3 (combined). No κ claim.

Kernel-checked Lean (Lean 4.33.0-rc1, pinned Mathlib; propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only; no `sorry`, no `native_decide`) with named hypotheses, in four groups.

**1. Premise narrowing for #7620** (the premises on which our #7623/#7630 κ is conditional). CLEAR certificates are sound and complete and every CLEAR is lossless (`ClearCert`); owned ascent is priced symmetrically, earns no credit, and relaxed-class floors imply strict-class floors (`OwnedAscent`); exact rows are equivalent to all columns (`NativeColumns`); the 981-pair census is a delta census, with kernel-checked inheritance from #7623 (`CensusComplete`); E1, E2 and E3 (flat and tree, under atomic calls) hold for the real owned skeleton of #7630 (`OwnedSkeleton`, `OwnedTree`). `PREMISES.md` lists per premise what is now a kernel fact and what is still assumed.

**2. Ceilings.**
- Caller side: cost closed form and the #7113 caller invoice (`CallerCost`); κ ≤ .0419448764 for rho = 2 two-arm callers under named hypotheses, with fully kernel-checked 2|2 (t ≥ 141/4096) and 1|1 (t ≥ 176/4096) bounds (`JointCeiling`).
- Whole word: **κ ≤ .0204110965 over legal (nested) words** (`WholeFloorNest.kappa_whole_floor_nested`). Hypotheses: Theorem Y (`h_Y`), slack-rank independence (`Indep`), the F-currency pricing link (`hF`) and `Priced`; the numeric cover is discharged in the kernel (`WholeFloorCover`, `NumCertK`). The verifier's nesting rule is what rules out lateral owned MOVEs (see FALSE.md item 11).
- **κ ≤ .0060197405 for class K(S22)** (`FloorK22`, `NumCertK22`), hypotheses: the rank input `ClassK22.rank_ge`, the cost-model links, and the caller-log input.
- **κ ≤ .0183952347 and κ ≤ .0134769139 for the restricted class M_V** (`CongestionI3*`), the second with descent mass ≥ 56. Hypotheses: the I3 path bound, the flag-DP minima, rank-8 decoders with C = 56 (exactly), and the public-provenance law. No known native lies in M_V, so these bound the restricted class, not the native class.
- Supporting: the 780-stop class-K LP certificate checked by `decide +kernel` (`FloorCert*`), descent pricing, helper D0 ≥ 2 ln 2 per paid stay (`FloorD0`).

**3. Word structure.** `Shadow` (the twin has the same net invoice, hence the same S, F, D0, κ), `Annihilator` (served ports ≤ descending owned rank), `Delivery` (net delivery needs two contacts with different courier rows; three genuine hops cost ≥ f(3); direct-read capacity), `DesignLaws`, `SharedCourier`, `PsiLaw`, `WordDuality` (legal words map to legal words, the Theorem-K invoice and roots are unchanged, P104 boundaries are self-dual), `PlaneLaws` (SPLIT for any n; QUARTER an exact partition for any n and block B containing 1; counts kernel-checked on E7 only), with `HubSettle`, `RankLaw`, `RankLawC`, `FrameSep`.

**4. Spec-break kills and small lemmas.** The rank, Gram and involution lemmas behind the kill arguments (`SpecTS`, `SpecGC`, `SpecRankP`, `SpecRankP2`, `SpecLemmaU`, `SpecLemmaU2`
